To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the jitter due to substrate and P/G coupling is proportional to the VCO gain, and that it can be reduced by increasing the supply voltage and the VCO gain.
the jitter in a CMOS phase-locked loop (PLL) is caused by substrate noise resulting from simultaneous switching and power/ ground noise.
a comprehensive stochastic model of substrate noise resulting from large-signal switching and P/G noise is presented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the jitter due to P/G noise in PLLs.
the analysis of the PLL jitter induced by P/G noise.
the analysis of the PLL jitter induced by P/G and substrate noise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the substrate noise is a major source for jitter in the VCO and the P/G noise has a negligible impact.
the substrate noise and P/G noise are two important noise sources which degrade the jitter performance of PLLs.
the P/G noise and substrate coupling are the major sources for the jitter in PLLs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed mathematical model is a powerful and accurate tool to study the jitter due to P/G noise and the substrate noise in a PLL.
the substrate noise and P/G noise can be reduced by using a proper layout technique and a low impedance P/G network, respectively.
a general stochastic analysis is developed to study the jitter due to substrate and P/G noises in PLLs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the P/G and substrate noise in VCOs can be significantly reduced by proper design and layout techniques.
the PLL jitter due the power/ground noise can be reduced by using a larger power supply and/or a larger power supply bypassing capacitance.
, in addition to the VCO, the PLL loop bandwidth and phase detector also contribute to the overall jitter.
